the use of immunohistochemical markers and molecular testing is important for the diagnosis and classification of hepatocellular tumors, and that molecular testing can provide additional information to the pathologist and the clinician.
The main takeaway from our work is that
immunohistochemistry is not sufficient to identify all H-HCA or b-HCA and that molecular testing is required to accurately subtype HCA.

mutational analysis is an important adjunct to the histologic diagnosis of hepatocellular neoplasms, and that it is important for pathologists to be familiar with the clinical implications of the various mutations that may be identified in hepatocellular lesions.
